working: Highest derivative is \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\), so the order is 2. Degree is defined only when the equation is a polynomial equation in the variables and derivatives; the terms \(\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{1/4}\) and \(x^{1/5}\) carry fractional powers, and clearing the quarter-power leaves \(\frac{dy}{dx}=\left(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+x^{1/5}\right)^{4}\) which is still non-polynomial because of \(x^{1/5}\). Hence order 2, degree not defined.
